newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico businessmen pledge $7 bln investment in '97.
newsitem.headline: Mexico businessmen pledge $7 bln investment in '97.

text.p: The Mexican Council of Businessmen, which groups 31 of the country's top business leaders, Tuesday promised President Ernesto Zedillo they would invest $7 billion in Mexico in 1997.
"We foresee making investments of $7 billion," Council leader Claudio X. Gonzalez said in a speech at the presidential residence of Los Pinos in Mexico City.
He said the investments would be directed into areas such as financial and commercial services, consumer durables, food, agriculture, soft drinks, beer and steel.
Last year, he said, the Council's pledge to invest $6.2 billion had been surpassed.
"We came through on what we offered, reaching the figure of $6.335 billion," Gonzalez said.

He said the investment pledge for 1997 was only a part of the investment planned by the private sector as a whole, and was independent of the amount more than 100 foreign business leaders will pledge to invest Wednesday.
